prerequisites: Principles of differential and integral calculus

learning_outcomes.text: is familiar with the initial basic ideas of quantum mechanics
is familiar with the experimental setups and tools that lead to these insights
is able to solve simple and conceptual problems based on specific quantum mechanical methods, without going deeply into the formal structure of the theory.

has understood the indispensable role that these new insights regarding quantum mechanics play in the developments of relatively new research domains, such as atomic physics, molecular physics and solid-state physics.
can understand some important models, research methods, and applications within the various research domains (see above) and explain the role of quantum mechanics therein.
can make connections across research domains and has developed a good intuition about the relevant length and energy scales that play a role in the different research domains and processes.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period

assessment_rules: This is an open book exam. The following materials are allowed during the exam: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, Cambridge University Press. NO notes taken in class or exercises. Calculator is allowed.
bibliography: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, third edition, Cambridge University Press
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
